lines.say: Zero to one hundred twenty-eight miles an hour, in three and a half seconds.
Kingda Ka was built for speed. The real challenge was stopping it.
Brake pads would wear out fast. So under every car sat rows of rare-earth magnets.
And on the track, thin copper fins.
When a magnet sweeps past a fin, it stirs up swirling electric currents inside the copper. Eddy currents.
Those currents create a magnetic field that pushes back, turning the train's speed into heat.
Nothing touches. Nothing wears out. No power needed.
If a launch fell short and the train rolled back, fins popped up to catch it.
Follow for how the world is really engineered.
